speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis. The chronic nature of your pain over several years, the specific location affecting weight-bearing joints like the hips and knees, and the pattern of pain worsening with activity while improving with rest are classic signs of degenerative joint disease. The involvement of the left great toe (likely hallux rigidus or osteoarthritis) further supports this, as inflammatory conditions like gout or rheumatoid arthritis typically present with different patterns, such as acute attacks or morning stiffness lasting longer than 30 minutes.
